title: A Hamilton dad died in Barton jail. What happened?
subtitle: Zakery Rogers died on Jan. 31, 2021
article: An inquest has been called into the death of Zakery Rogers, who died more than four years ago while incarcerated at the Hamilton-Wentworth Detention Centre.
Dr. Karen Schiff, regional supervising coroner, announced the inquest Tuesday. It is mandatory because the 26-year-old died while in custody.
The inquest - with dates and times to be announced later - will examine the circumstances of his death.
The Spectator has reported extensively on Rogers' death and his sister Kylee Rogers' push for answers and work to support others who struggled like her brother.
Zak struggled with addiction and mental health, ultimately leading to homelessness and jail. Family would take him to hospital, only to see him released soon after.

After he was arrested in early 2020, he was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and manic depression. He was doing well on medication, so Kylee agreed to be his surety and helped him get bail. But after being released from Maplehurst Correctional Complex in Milton that Christmas Eve, Zak's prescriptions weren't accessible over the holidays. He spiralled and ran away New Year's Eve.
When he was arrested again about a month later, Kylee was initially relieved because she believed her brother would get help. Instead, she got a phone call on Jan. 31, 2021, that he had died.
She initially believed his death was an overdose, but the autopsy was inconclusive.

The jury at the inquest will hear from witnesses and experts and will come to a verdict on his cause and manner of death. The jury can also make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths in the future.
